author: independent critic pair for the React course-final MCQ (education and React 19 / react-router SME; one review session covering both roles; did not author the bank), 2026-11-19. Reviewed final-mcq.gift 9c1df201 (public-answer header version of candidate 2746e653) and blueprint.json 20c684dc. Verdict: approve, 0 high, 0 medium, 5 low. Education scope: key, distractors, taught scope (react/*/*/artifact.html), difficulty, cueing, overlap, blueprint objectives, counts and duration. Findings are RCFE-1 to RCFE-5.

findings.claim: The deciding fact, that an id must be unique so two labels cannot point at the same input, is not stated in accessible-forms, which teaches only that htmlFor must match the input's id. The item is answerable by inference and option C is the only fix that works, so it is a mild transfer, not an untaught fact.
findings.recommendation: Optional: add one unique-id sentence to the accessible-forms topic, or keep as a transfer item. No bank change required.

findings.claim: Sampling is acceptable for a 30-item final: every one of the 26 topics has at least one item, 46 of 75 objectives are decided or co-decided, all 46 blueprint objective ids exist in the catalog with no duplicates and objectiveFormats keys equal objectives. The 29 untested objectives are mostly o1/o2 recall-level ones that the topic banks and module labs cover. Thin spots: loading-data-with-useeffect o1/o2 (fetch in an Effect, dependency array; q16 tests only cleanup and Strict Mode) and usestate o1/o2. The item-to-objective map is author-tagged in the checks note, not in the blueprint, so the blueprint cannot show which item decides which objective.
findings.recommendation: None required. Optional: when the bank is next edited, tag or add one dependency-array item.

findings.claim: Band and distractor quality. q18 reads easy: B, C and D (front end sends the profile, a VITE_ variable turns Spring off, a cached line) are structurally implausible against the stem. q27 is the standard null guard taught in conditional-display and sits in the hard band; q13 (defaultValue) is easy. Weak distractors: q05 C (randomUUID can repeat), q14 B (rename the Hook), q16 C (an empty array runs every render). Not cueing keys: the key is the strictly longest option in only 2 of 30, key positions are A8 B7 C7 D8 with no repeated run (a DACB/ADCB rotation from q13 on, not exploitable).
findings.recommendation: Optional: re-band q13/q18/q27 or harden q18 and the three weak distractors.

location.selector: bank vs topic banks, checkpoint, legacy module check

findings.claim: Overlap. No item is copied from a topic artifact.gift (highest lexical overlap 0.20, q02 vs project-structure o1, a scenario version of the same entry-chain fact) or from checkpoint-mcq.gift (highest 0.27, q09 vs sfcp-q20). Shared deciding facts remain: q25 and sfcp-q26 (a component outside a provider reads the default), q11 and sfcp-q21 (render snapshot and updater), q09 and sfcp-q20 (HTML error body, parse versus res.ok), and in the bank q23 and q29 (state in a private copy instead of the provider's state). The legacy web-and-react-module-check keeps only its blueprint here; it shares 18 of its 21 React objective ids with this blueprint, but its question bank is not in the repository, so item overlap and the bank header's claim of being distinct from it cannot be checked.
findings.recommendation: None for this release. If the legacy module-check bank is landed later, de-duplicate against it. Surfaces and deciding steps differ enough that the checkpoint pairs are not blocking.

findings.claim: Duration. 30 items in 30 minutes meets the contract in course-final-gift.test.mjs (30 items, at least one minute per item). The bank carries 2360 words, about 78 per item, and 20 items with code. At 175 words per minute the reading takes about 13.5 minutes, leaving about 33 seconds per item to decide, and the trace items (q11, q16, q24, q26, q30) need more. No learner timing exists.
findings.recommendation: Owner decision: keep 30 minutes, or allow more. Non-blocking.
